alerts.title: Low phosphate with TDF suggests tubular toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list tubular wasting syndrome as a known adverse effect of TDF. Patient on TDF for 6 years with serum phosphate 0.78 mmol/L, trace proteinuria, and creatinine 112 umol/L. Hypophosphataemia and proteinuria together are consistent with proximal tubular dysfunction from TDF. Evidence against drug attribution: trace proteinuria may be secondary to uncontrolled hypertension, and occupational musculoskeletal symptoms could explain thigh heaviness independently. However, the combination of low phosphate and proteinuria on TDF warrants evaluation for Fanconi syndrome. No phosphate monitoring was ordered.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate renal tubular function (urine phosphate, fractional phosphate excretion) and consider switching TDF to TAF if tubular wasting confirmed.

alerts.title: TDF plus ibuprofen and hypertension increases renal risk
alerts.message: Guidelines note TDF can cause renal failure and that patients on TDF admitted to hospital should have creatinine checked because intercurrent illness with dehydration may worsen renal function. Patient has uncontrolled hypertension (146/94), trace proteinuria, and uses over-the-counter ibuprofen regularly for chronic back pain. TDF nephrotoxicity risk is compounded by NSAID use and hypertension. The 6-month follow-up interval without renal monitoring between visits may be excessive given these combined risk factors.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess eGFR and renal tubular markers now. Limit ibuprofen use; consider alternative analgesia. Increase renal monitoring frequency given combined nephrotoxic risks.

alerts.title: Uncontrolled BP on amlodipine with missed doses
alerts.message: Guidelines list lower limb oedema, headache, and palpitations as side effects of amlodipine. Patient has BP 146/94 despite amlodipine 5 mg, with admitted missed doses during travel. Trace proteinuria may reflect hypertensive nephropathy. The plan refills the same dose without escalation or urinalysis follow-up. No assessment of target organ damage beyond dipstick was ordered. Persistent uncontrolled hypertension with proteinuria increases cardiovascular and renal risk, compounding TDF nephrotoxicity.

evidence.recommended_action: Titrate antihypertensive therapy (increase amlodipine or add agent), reinforce adherence strategies, and arrange BP follow-up sooner than 6 months.

alerts.title: EFV-based regimen long-term — consider modernisation
alerts.message: Patient has been on TDF/3TC/EFV for 6 years with viral suppression and CD4 of 540. Current guidelines recommend monitoring creatinine/eGFR at 3, 6, and then 6–12 monthly intervals for TDF. No eGFR value is documented despite creatinine of 112 umol/L. EFV is associated with neuropsychiatric and metabolic effects; after 6 years, a regimen review for potential modernisation to better-tolerated agents may be warranted, particularly given new musculoskeletal complaints.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate and document eGFR. Consider regimen review for EFV modernisation given long-term use and stable virological status.
